# Check If N and Its Double Exist.

@example -8 is twice -4, and it may come before -4 just as well as after it.
[-8,5,3,-4]
=> true

@example The 0 would have to pair with itself, and none of 5, 9 and 3 is twice another.
[0,5,9,3]
=> false

@example The two 0s sit at different places, and 0 is twice 0.
[7,0,1,0]
=> true

# The shortest arrays: a pair in either order, and no pair.
[3,6]
=> true

[6,3]
=> true

[2,3]
=> false

# Two 0s, and a lone 0 beside another number.
[0,0]
=> true

[0,1]
=> false

# A number repeated is not twice itself.
[-7,5,-7,5]
=> false

# Odd numbers next to what integer division would call their halves,
# with the "half" both after and before the odd number, for both signs.
[9,4,-4,-9,6,13,-11,-5]
=> false

# A number and minus twice it don't pair.
[3,-6,-5,10]
=> false

# At the bounds: twice 1000 is out of range, and -1000 is twice -500.
[1000,-1000]
=> false

[-500,999,-1000]
=> true

# The doubles 1000 and -1000, at the edges of the range, placed before
# their halves 500 and -500.
[1000,-999,500]
=> true

[-1000,999,-500]
=> true

# The only pair is in the last two places.
[1,3,7,9,11,13,17,40,20]
=> true

# The longest array, odd numbers only: no pair.

=> false

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 2 small
[3,10,10,-5,7,12]
=> false

@gen 3 small
[9,-8,10,-6,10,3,-4,7]
=> true

@gen 8 small
[11,15,15,0,0,5,-1,9]
=> true

@gen 10 small
[29,-21,-11,-9,-1,15,-1,-19]
=> false

@gen 13 small
[-5,-13,-5,0,3,5,-3,-3]
=> false

@gen 17 small
[6,9,-1,3,-5,-13,-9]
=> true

@gen 19 small
[-8,-4]
=> true

@gen 20 small
[5,3,-5,-11]
=> false
